newsitem.title: FRANCE: French govt to present revised budget on Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: French govt to present revised budget on Wednesday.

text.p: The French government will present a revised budget for 1996 on Wednesday designed to keep the central government budget deficit on target at 288 billion French francs ($56.95 billion), an official said on Tuesday.
Government officials have declined comment on the contents of the revised budget, which is traditionally presented at the end of the year to ensure deficit-cutting programmes stay on course.
Financial daily Les Echos said last week, however, the government was considering new spending cuts to make up for lower-than-expected revenues and higher spending elsewhere.
The government has pledged to reduce the total public deficit this year to four percent of gross domestic product (GDP) and to three percent of GDP next year from five percent last year.
Les Echos said the government was also considering whether to save funds by paying telephone bills to France Telecom after its change of status on January 1 rather than before.
